Subject: Marketplace listing pricing — can Redwood match competitor credit?

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. BrightLayer is moving quickly on this pilot and we have one final procurement ask before we can sign — a marketplace-focused promotional credit to match a competitive offer our procurement team favors.

High-level: they want an effective blended discount that reduces first-year cost by ~12–15% on our proposed SKU mix. We prefer to go via the AWS Marketplace listing (co-sell) so we can keep procurement simple.

Attached is our RFP summary and expected seat/usage profile for year one. Can Redwood accommodate a one-time promotional credit applied through the marketplace listing, or would this need to be a private offer outside the public SKU? If outside, please flag any timing or procurement blockers.

We'd like to close by end of next week — procurement is waiting on final verification.

Best,

Lauren — forwarding for Deal Desk review. Key facts:
- ARR profile (yr1): $420k ARR (mix of seat + token-based ingestion) — see RFP.
- BrightLayer wants ~12–15% first-year effective reduction applied at marketplace level.
- Preferred route: private offer via AWS Marketplace (co-sell) so procurement sign-off is straightforward.

Proposal I'm comfortable with: 12% promotional credit applied as a one-time marketplace allowance for the first 12 months, with standard list pricing thereafter. Redwood would treat this as a marketing/promotional credit (not a change to list price). If AWS requires split for co-sell incentives, we propose Redwood absorbs 8% and AWS co-sell covers 4% (subject to PM approval).

Attached: proposed-pricing-split.xlsx (simple model + expected unit economics).

Can Deal Desk approve the 12% across the marketplace path? If not, what steps to get an exception approved quickly (who signs off, and SLA for decision)?

—Ben

Thanks for the details. A few quick questions before I escalate to pricing approvals:

1) Confirmed effective ARR math to validate 12% not materially impacting expected unit economics? (Ben, your workbook helps but we need a banded sensitivity).
2) We need AWS Partner Manager alignment if we're expecting AWS to credit 4% co-sell. Emma — can you confirm AWS's ability to commit to a short-term promotional co-sell credit and any internal review steps?
3) Timeline: if BrightLayer needs DocuSign + AWS review, we should expect a 5–7 business day window for private offer publishing in the marketplace.

If AWS confirms, I can route a provisional approval for 12% (with finance sign-off) and ship a private offer template. If AWS declines the credit, we can do a Redwood-only promotional credit but will need an executive approval for delta >10%.

Looping Emma to validate the AWS side.

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@amazon.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Turner <sam.turner@brightlayer.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: Marketplace listing pricing — private offer vs promo credit?

Hi Lauren / team — thanks for the context.

Short answer: AWS can support a time-limited promotional credit routed via a private offer, but it requires a Partner Manager sign-off and our internal marketplace promotions team will need to review the ROI rationale. We typically approve promotional credits up to ~10% faster; requests above that (12%–15%) need a sponsor and business case.

From my side I can commit to supporting a 4% co-sell contribution (as part of the overall promo) pending completion of our review (1–3 business days) and a short justification note that we can provide jointly to the marketplace promotions team. If Redwood covers 8% and AWS 4%, that aligns with our internal thresholds and I can expedite.

Next steps:
- Redwood: send sensitivity band (ben_carter) & short business case (1–2 paragraphs) showing lift + expected close timeline.
- BrightLayer: confirm willingness to accept a private offer and timeline to sign.

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Emma
AWS Partner Manager

Sam — good news. Based on the Deal Desk review + AWS PM feedback we're able to offer a one-time promotional credit applied via an AWS private offer as follows:

- Promotional structure: 12% effective reduction for first 12 months on the agreed SKU mix.
- Split: Redwood contribution = 8% (marketing/promo reserve), AWS contribution = 4% (pending Partner Manager final signoff).
- Conditions: private offer route; BrightLayer signs the private offer DocuSign link and we publish once AWS promotions team approves (target 3–5 business days).

Next steps:
1) Ben will upload the private offer template and final pricing to the HubSpot deal this afternoon.
2) BrightLayer (Sam/procurement) to confirm acceptance and return the signed DocuSign PO.
3) Emma to complete AWS internal review and confirm the 4% co-sell contribution.

Sam — if you can confirm acceptance by EOD Monday we'll prioritize the publishing queue and aim to have the private offer live within the week.

Thanks everyone — excited to close this.

Sofia Ivanova
